content: The QTc interval should be closely monitored when using drugs that may prolong it. If possible, avoid coadministration or use an alternative medication. If coadministration cannot be avoided, obtain ECGs at the initiation of therapy, during concurrent use, and as clinically indicated. Discontinue the drug if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. Givosiran increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP2D6 substrates or reduce their dosage according to product labeling. Chloroquine and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. Goserelin increases chloroquine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine and granisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as the antibody response may be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy discontinuation if immune competence is restored. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism and increases its toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A vaccine, hepatitis A/B vaccine, hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine, and hepatitis B vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Histrelin increases chloroquine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus vaccine (nonavalent) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at doses exceeding physiological levels), may reduce immune responses to vaccines. Monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of hydrocodone and hydromorphone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to its total analgesic effect. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of hydroxychloroquine sulfate by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Chloroquine and hydroxyzine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ibutilide by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor; avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of iloperidone by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, while iloperidone increases chloroquine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine also increases iloperidone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of imipramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of indacaterol (inhaled) and indapamide by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of influenza virus vaccines (quadrivalent, cell-cultured; quadrivalent, intranasal; trivalent; trivalent, adjuvanted; trivalent, recombinant) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug for trivalent, adjuvanted vaccines. Monitor closely for recombinant vaccines. Immune response to vaccines may be reduced in immunocompromised individuals. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of inotuzumab by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiating any QTc-prolonging drug, and monitor periodically as clinically indicated. Chloroquine and isoflurane both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of isradipine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Both drugs decrease the QTc interval. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the Japanese encephalitis virus vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lanthanum carbonate decreases chloroquine levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer chloroquine at least two hours before or after lanthanum. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lapatinib by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within nine months after its last subcutaneous dose, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Chloroquine and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. Leuprolide increases chloroquine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, raising the risk of torsades de pointes. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine and levalbuterol both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Chloroquine and lithium both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lofexidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lonafarnib increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. Chloroquine and loperamide both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lopinavir by prolonging the QTc interval. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Lorcaserin increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of lumefantrine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Magaldrate decreases chloroquine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least four hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Magnesium hydroxide decreases chloroquine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate doses by at least four hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Magnesium oxide decreases chloroquine levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Separate doses by at least four hours. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of maprotiline by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine (live) and the measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella vaccine (live) through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Chloroquine and mefloquine are contraindicated due to an unknown mechanism. Chloroquine increases mefloquine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Chloroquine reduces the efficacy of the meningococcal ACYW-135 polysaccharide vaccine and the meningococcal group B vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Individuals with altered immune competence may have reduced immune responses to the vaccine. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of methadone by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of methamphetamine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of metoprolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine and midostaurin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Chloroquine increases mifepristone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Mirabegron increases the levels or effects of chloroquine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine and mirtazapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Mitotane decreases chloroquine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of moxifloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Chloroquine increases the levels or effects of nebivolol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
